intent: Trace the global temperature anomaly relative to the 1951-1980 average over the full series and compare its early and recent periods.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Does the chart trace the global temperature anomaly over the full series and compare its early and recent periods?
The recent period of the series has higher temperature anomalies than the early period; for example, the last value (0.946 °C) is greater than the first value (-0.156 °C).

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The global temperature anomaly relative to the 1951-1980 average shows an overall increasing trend from the first point (-0.156 °C) to the last point (0.946 °C) across the full series.
units.computation: Compare first value (-0.156) to last value (0.946); the series rises over time.
accept: The line ends higher than it starts, indicating warming.
Overall upward trend from start to end.
reject: The series shows no overall change.

units.claim: The recent period of the series has higher temperature anomalies than the early period; for example, the last value (0.946 °C) is greater than the first value (-0.156 °C).
units.computation: Compare early value at point_order 1 (-0.156) with recent value at point_order 137 (0.946); recent is higher.
accept: Recent temperatures are higher than early temperatures.
The end of the series is warmer than the beginning.
reject: Early and recent periods are equal.
Recent period is cooler than early period.

optional_valid: Mentioning the minimum value (-0.432 °C) as part of the early period context.
Noting that the maximum value (0.946 °C) occurs at the last point.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the temperature change.
Specific decade averages not directly computable from the provided rows.
review_notes: The intent asks to trace the full series and compare early and recent periods; two semantic units cover the trend and the early-recent comparison.
Only first and last points are used as minimal evidence for the trend and comparison; intermediate points are not required.
